3 Model Architecture

Most competitive neural sequence transduction models have an encoder-decoder structure [5, 2, 35]. Here, the encoder maps an input sequence of symbol representations (x1,...,xn) to a sequence of continuous representations z = (z1,...,zn). Given z, the decoder then generates an output sequence (y1,...,ym) of symbols one element at a time. At each step the model is auto-regressive [10], consuming the previously generated symbols as additional input when generating the next.

# SEARCHABLE DESCRIPTION: Transformer Model Variations Ablation Study (Section 6.2)

## DOCUMENT OVERVIEW
This content describes **Section 6.2 "Model Variations"** from the original Transformer paper ("Attention Is All You Need" by Vaswani et al.). It presents comprehensive ablation experiments evaluating the importance of different architectural components of the Transformer model on **English-to-German translation** using the **newstest2013 development set**. Experiments use **beam search** without checkpoint averaging.

---

## KEY FACTS, NUMBERS, AND DATA POINTS

### BASE MODEL CONFIGURATION (Reference)
| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| **N (layers)** | 6 |
| **d_model** | 512 |
| **d_ff (feed-forward dim)** | 2048 |
| **h (attention heads)** | 8 |
| **d_k (key dim)** | 64 |
| **d_v (value dim)** | 64 |
| **P_drop (dropout)** | 0.1 |
| **ε_ls (label smoothing)** | 0.1 |
| **Train steps** | 100K |
| **PPL (dev)** | 4.92 |
| **BLEU (dev)** | 25.8 |
| **Parameters** | 65M |

### VARIATION (A): NUMBER OF ATTENTION HEADS & KEY/VALUE DIMENSIONS
*Computation kept constant (as per Section 3.2.2)*

| h (heads) | d_k | d_v | PPL | BLEU | Params (M) | Notes |
|-----------|-----|-----|-----|------|------------|-------|
| 1 | 512 | 512 | 5.29 | 24.9 | - | Single-head: **0.9 BLEU worse** than best |
| 4 | 128 | 128 | 5.00 | 25.5 | - | |
| 8 | 64 | 64 | 4.91 | 25.8 | - | **Base model (best)** |
| 16 | 32 | 32 | 5.01 | 25.4 | - | |
| 32 | 16 | 16 | 5.01 | 25.4 | - | Quality drops with too many heads |

**Key Finding**: Single-head attention is **0.9 BLEU worse** than optimal 8-head setting. Quality degrades with excessive heads (32 heads).

### VARIATION (B): ATTENTION KEY SIZE (d_k)
*Reducing d_k hurts model quality*

| d_k | PPL | BLEU | Params (M) |
|-----|-----|------|------------|
| 16 | 5.16 | 25.1 | 58 |
| 32 | 5.01 | 25.4 | 60 |
| 64 (base) | 4.91 | 25.8 | 65 |

**Key Finding**: Smaller d_k degrades performance. Suggests **determining compatibility is not easy** and **more sophisticated compatibility function than dot product may be beneficial**.

### VARIATION (C): MODEL SIZE (LAYERS, d_model, d_ff)

#### Varying Number of Layers (N)
| N | PPL | BLEU | Params (M) |
|---|-----|------|------------|
| 2 | 6.11 | 23.7 | 36 |
| 4 | 5.19 | 25.3 | 50 |
| 6 (base) | 4.88 | 25.5 | 80 |
| 8 | 4.66 | 26.0 | 168 |

#### Varying d_model (with corresponding d_k, d_v)
| d_model | d_k=d_v | PPL | BLEU | Params (M) |
|---------|---------|-----|------|------------|
| 256 | 32 | 5.75 | 24.5 | 28 |
| 512 (base) | 64 | 4.88 | 25.5 | 80 |
| 1024 | 128 | 4.66 | 26.0 | 168 |

#### Varying d_ff (feed-forward dimension)
| d_ff | PPL | BLEU | Params (M) |
|------|-----|------|------------|
| 1024 | 5.12 | 25.4 | 53 |
| 2048 (base) | 4.88 | 25.5 | 80 |
| 4096 | 4.75 | 26.2 | 90 |

**Key Finding**: **Bigger models are better** - increasing layers, d_model, or d_ff improves BLEU and reduces perplexity.

### VARIATION (D): DROPOUT RATE (P_drop)
| P_drop | ε_ls | PPL | BLEU |
|--------|------|-----|------|
| 0.0 | 0.1 | 5.77 | 24.6 |
| 0.2 | 0.1 | 4.95 | 25.5 |
| 0.1 | 0.0 | 4.67 | 25.3 |
| 0.1 | 0.2 | 5.47 | 25.7 |

**Key Finding**: **Dropout is very helpful in avoiding over-fitting**. P_drop=0.0 significantly hurts performance (PPL 5.77 vs 4.92, BLEU 24.6 vs 25.8).

### VARIATION (E): POSITIONAL ENCODING
| Type | PPL | BLEU |
|------|-----|------|
| Sinusoidal (base) | 4.92 | 25.8 |
| Learned positional embeddings [9] | 4.92 | 25.7 |

**Key Finding**: **Nearly identical results** - learned positional embeddings perform equivalently to sinusoidal positional encoding.

### BIG MODEL CONFIGURATION
| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| **N** | 6 |
| **d_model** | 1024 |
| **d_ff** | 4096 |
| **h** | 16 |
| **P_drop** | 0.3 |
| **Train steps** | 300K |
| **PPL (dev)** | 4.33 |
| **BLEU (dev)** | 26.4 |
| **Parameters** | 213M |

**Improvement over base**: +0.6 BLEU, -0.59 PPL, 3.3× parameters

# SEARCHABLE DESCRIPTION: Transformer Model Regularization Techniques and Performance Benchmarks

## DOCUMENT OVERVIEW
This content covers **Section 5.4 Regularization** from the "Attention Is All You Need" paper (Vaswani et al., 2017), detailing three regularization techniques used during Transformer model training, plus **Table 2** comparing BLEU scores and training computational costs (FLOPs) across multiple machine translation models on English-to-German (EN-DE) and English-to-French (EN-FR) newstest2014 benchmarks.

---

## KEY FACTS, NUMBERS, AND DATA POINTS

### Regularization Techniques (Section 5.4)

| Technique | Parameter Value | Application Details |
|-----------|----------------|---------------------|
| **Residual Dropout** | Pdrop = 0.1 (base model) | Applied to output of each sub-layer before residual addition and normalization; also applied to sums of embeddings + positional encodings in both encoder and decoder stacks |
| **Label Smoothing** | εls = 0.1 | Applied during training; hurts perplexity (model learns to be more unsure) but improves accuracy and BLEU score |
| **Third Technique** | Not explicitly named in excerpt | Text says "We employ three types of regularization" but only two are detailed in provided content |

### Model Performance Comparison (Table 2) - EN-DE BLEU Scores

| Model | EN-DE BLEU | Training Cost (FLOPs) EN-DE |
|-------|------------|----------------------------|
| ByteNet [18] | 23.75 | Not specified |
| GNMT + RL [38] | 24.6 | 2.3 × 10¹⁹ |
| ConvS2S [9] | 25.16 | 9.6 × 10¹⁸ |
| MoE [32] | 26.03 | 2.0 × 10¹⁹ |
| GNMT + RL Ensemble [38] | 26.30 | 1.8 × 10²⁰ |
| ConvS2S Ensemble [9] | 26.36 | 7.7 × 10¹⁹ |
| **Transformer (base model)** | **27.3** | **3.3 × 10¹⁸** |
| **Transformer (big)** | **28.4** | **2.3 × 10¹⁹** |

### Model Performance Comparison (Table 2) - EN-FR BLEU Scores

| Model | EN-FR BLEU | Training Cost (FLOPs) EN-FR |
|-------|------------|----------------------------|
| Deep-Att + PosUnk [39] | 39.2 | 1.0 × 10²⁰ |
| GNMT + RL [38] | 39.92 | 1.4 × 10²⁰ |
| ConvS2S [9] | 40.46 | 1.5 × 10²⁰ |
| MoE [32] | 40.56 | 1.2 × 10²⁰ |
| Deep-Att + PosUnk Ensemble [39] | 40.4 | 8.0 × 10²⁰ |
| GNMT + RL Ensemble [38] | 41.16 | 1.1 × 10²¹ |
| ConvS2S Ensemble [9] | 41.29 | 1.2 × 10²¹ |
| **Transformer (base model)** | **38.1** | **Not fully specified (3.3 × 10¹⁸ for EN-DE)** |
| **Transformer (big)** | **41.8** | **2.3 × 10¹⁹** |

### Key Performance Insights
- **Transformer (big)** achieves **28.4 BLEU EN-DE** and **41.8 BLEU EN-FR** - highest single-model scores
- **Transformer (base)** achieves **27.3 BLEU EN-DE** at only **3.3 × 10¹⁸ FLOPs** - dramatically lower training cost
- Transformer base model uses **~7-30x fewer FLOPs** than previous state-of-the-art single models
- Transformer big model outperforms all ensembles on EN-DE (28.4 vs 26.36) and nearly matches best ensemble on EN-FR (41.8 vs 41.29)
- **Training cost efficiency**: Transformer base is ~7x cheaper than ConvS2S (9.6e18 vs 3.3e18 FLOPs) while achieving higher BLEU
